question: How many rights are mentioned under “Right to Equality”?
solution:
The correct answer is** __5__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The right to equality is one of the **five fundamental rights in the Indian constitution, **which are:

 
 
• This right of equality in **law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of race, religion, gender, and caste or birthplace**.
 
• It also includes** equality of opportunity in matters of employment and abolition of untouchability and titles**.
 
• In a few words, it can be said that it is the right to live with equal opportunities.
 
• It implies treating all people in the same way and nobody can be treated privileged that may dishonor any individual or group.
 
• Article no 14 of our constitution, it guarantees that all people shall be equally protected by the laws of the country. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Article 14 **provides for equality in general. 
 
• **Article 21 **guarantees the right to life and liberty.
 
• Article 15 prohibits Page 14 14 discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• This concept is borrowed from British Constitution.
